newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Toys R Us sees growth in baby market.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Toys R Us sees growth in baby market.

text.p: Toys R Us Inc, which pioneered the concept of megastores for children's products, intends to develop the market for the infant and toddler's merchandise through its $376 million stock purchase of Baby Superstore Inc.
Toys R Us Chief Executive Michael Goldstein on Wednesday said the world's biggest retailer of children's products plans a speedy expansion of Baby Superstore.

"We will have about 80 (baby) stores when the combination occurs. Next year, there will be some digestion, so we will only add 15 or 20 stores. But then we'll add maybe 40 to 50 stores a year," Goldstein told Reuters.
Toys R Us said earlier it agreed to buy Baby Superstore Inc in a stock merger valued at about $376 million.
Goldstein said the deal will add to Toys R Us' bottom line and should improve its overall growth rate as well.

"We expect it will add to earnings next year. In terms of earnings per share, it should be pretty neutral next year, and then after that it should add to earnings and earnings per share," Goldstein said.
The deal would make Baby Superstore Chairman Jack Tate the biggest individual shareholder in Toys R Us, he said.

"We plan to use all of our expertise over the years in the juvenile business and combine it. ...We think the superstore is the way to go, when well executed. When you create a superstore, you add to the market," Goldstein said.
Toys R Us Chief Financial Officer Louis Lipschitz said the company did not believe it would face any regulatory obstacles to completing the acquisition.
He said the share ratio was fixed in the agreement, so a "collar" on the value of the stock to be received by Baby Superstore shareholders was not necessary.
When asked if Toys R Us was pursuing any other possible acquisitions, he said, "We are always looking for new opportunities."
